I grew up in a household where we did not have cattle. When the farming season came, we would take a take rope and hold it straight, whilst others dug holes adjacent to the rope. New agricultural or NRM practices
• CONSERVATIVE AGRICULTURE
• Using a planter
• Using herbicides for weeding and not hoes
• Conservation agriculture
• Making lines using ripper
• Conserving soil using lime. It controls soil erosion and the soil becomes firmer
• Crop rotation
• NATURAL RESOURCES MANAGEMENT
• Avoiding deforestation and using coal for curing tobacco
• Avoiding stream bank cultivation
• Avoiding veld fires
• Avoiding pulling logs along the road. They cause soil erosion
• LIVESTOCK PRACTICES
• Cattle dipping and vaccination
• Conserving maize stalks for cattle feed

Most important for the women of the community (top 2)
• 1.Conservation agriculture
• 2.Vaccination of cattle

Most important for the men of the community (top 2)
• 1. Use of herbicides
• 2. Vaccination and dipping of cattle
WOMEN
1. Conservation Agriculture
It reduces labor and saves time
The planter is programmed to put adequate seed and fertilizer at the same time which saves time and labor. The quantities are consistent
The yield is very high due to adequately measured fertilizer
The plants are well spaced and the plants grow very healthy
The germination rate is very good.
2. Vaccination of cattle
Vaccination of cattle protects them from ticks and they remain healthy
If the cattle are vaccinated and dipped they do not get sick often.
Cattle are a source of wealth so there is need to prioritize the cattle
MEN
1. Use of herbicides
Reduces labor of hoe weeding
The crop is not disturbed by weeds such as the witch weed.
The yield will be higher especially when the field is clear off the weeds that may be a threat
2. Vaccination and cattle dipping

Yes we still follow them. Women are responsible for hoe weeding, planting the seeds, dehusking the maize cobs and winnowing the maize
